verdicts.decision_note: The reported zero ticket, referral, and earnings values establish the dashboard requirement to display earned reward-accounting data accurately.
First concrete failure: the dashboard displayed zero tickets, referrals, and earnings despite prior referral activity.
Distinct partial-accounting state: dashboard and NFT reward views showed conflicting earnings, zero tickets, and a malformed $5,000,000 value.
Distinct aggregate-view path: leaderboard and homepage referral totals remained zero while the NFT-linked view reported referral activity.
Target-specific implementation claim that referral, ticket, earnings, and per-NFT accounting values had been corrected.
First concrete failure of the no-referral path: seven mints produced only four accounted tickets and commissions.
Target-specific implementation claim that missing ticket and commission records were backfilled for existing NFTs.
Post-fix persistence: the leaderboard still showed only four tickets and four commissions after the claimed backfill.
Target-specific implementation claim that the missing ticket and commission issue was fixed for testing with new mints.
Post-fix persistence on a new no-referral mint: its ticket and commission were still absent from the leaderboard.
The client defines the system accounting rule that each mint produces a paired ticket and $5 commission across code-used and no-referral reward paths.
Distinct partial outcome: code-used accounting and recent random tickets worked, but historical tickets and no-referral commissions remained missing.

value_updates.expected_aggregate_rule: Going forward, each mint must be represented by one ticket and one $5 commission in reward-accounting views, whether a referral code is used or the reward is randomly assigned.

verdicts.decision_note: The client removes the historical data-backfill obligation while retaining prospective ticket-and-commission accounting behavior.
The client accepts the executable accounting exception that the first mint cannot award a ticket or commission because no prior NFT exists.
Target-specific implementation claim that temporary backend logic was added to reflect tickets and commissions correctly.
First concrete post-fix verification of aggregate accounting: the leaderboard showed eleven tickets and eleven commissions under the accepted first-mint exception.
